title: Zero-Downtime Database Schema Migrations in Production with Drizzle ORM and PostgreSQL
seoTitle: Zero-Downtime PostgreSQL Migrations with Drizzle ORM
description: Learn how to perform safe, zero-downtime database schema migrations in PostgreSQL using Drizzle ORM without locking tables or breaking live apps.

author.name: Aafaque Nazir
author.bio: Independent web engineer building high-performance websites, e-commerce stores, and SaaS web applications for clients across India & worldwide.

quickAnswer: Zero-downtime database migrations in PostgreSQL are achieved by breaking breaking-changes into backward-compatible multi-step deployments, avoiding exclusive table locks, and managing Drizzle ORM state changes incrementally.

faqs.question: How do you avoid table locks during PostgreSQL migrations?
faqs.answer: Avoid heavy operations like adding columns with default values or modifying column types directly on large tables. Instead, add nullable columns, backfill data in small batches, and apply constraints later.

faqs.question: Can Drizzle ORM run zero-downtime migrations automatically?
faqs.answer: Drizzle generates precise SQL migration files, but safely executing them without downtime requires discipline. You must use the expand-and-contract pattern and separate schema deployment from application logic updates.

faqs.question: What is the best way to rename a column in production?
faqs.answer: Rename operations cause downtime if old code queries the old name. Use the expand-and-contract pattern: add the new column, write to both columns via application code, backfill historical data, read from the new column, and finally drop the old column.

sections.text: When running high-traffic applications, deploying a database change is often the rishest part of the release cycle. Simple commands like `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` or changing a column type can take an exclusive lock on PostgreSQL tables, freezing all read and write queries until the operation completes. For systems handling heavy traffic, such as the [Inventory Management / InvMaster OS](/projects/1/), unexpected table locks lead to dropped requests, frontend timeouts, and angry users.

Drizzle ORM provides a fast, lightweight bridge to PostgreSQL. While Drizzle Kit makes generating SQL migration scripts simple, developers must still follow strict engineering rules to ensure updates happen live without disrupting users.

To achieve zero downtime, break every significant schema change into multiple separate deployments using the expand-and-contract pattern. Never deploy a breaking schema change and application code update in the exact same release.

items: Phase 1 (Expand): Add new database columns or tables as optional fields so existing code continues working.
Phase 2 (Migrate): Update application code to write to both old and new fields while reading from the old ones.
Phase 3 (Backfill): Run a background script to copy historical data from old fields to new fields.
Phase 4 (Switch): Update application code to read exclusively from the new fields.
Phase 5 (Contract): Remove old columns or tables in a subsequent release after verifying stability.

sections.title: Engineering Rule
sections.text: Never use `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'value'` on existing large tables in PostgreSQL unless you are running newer PostgreSQL versions (11+) that optimize metadata-only defaults. Always add columns as nullable first, backfill in batches, and apply the constraint later.

Adding a foreign key constraint forces PostgreSQL to scan the entire table and lock writes to verify existing rows. To prevent this, create the foreign key as `NOT VALID`, which tells PostgreSQL to skip checking existing rows immediately. Then, validate the constraint in a separate transaction.

sections.caption: Adding a non-blocking foreign key in PostgreSQL
sections.code:
-- Step 1: Add constraint without validating existing rows
ALTER TABLE shipments
ADD CONSTRAINT fk_warehouse
FOREIGN KEY (warehouse_id)
REFERENCES warehouses(id)
NOT VALID;

-- Step 2: Validate constraint later without exclusive locks
ALTER TABLE shipments
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_warehouse;
